sources.entry: Backrest | Web UI and orchestrator for restic backups

summary.one_liner: Backrest is a web UI and background orchestrator built on top of the restic backup tool, for creating repos, scheduling snapshots, and browsing or restoring files.
summary.what_it_does: Backrest wraps the restic CLI in a WebUI for creating repositories, browsing snapshots, and restoring files. It can run in the background to schedule snapshots and run repo maintenance operations such as prune, check, and forget on a cron-style schedule. It can import existing restic repositories and supports pre/post backup shell command hooks. Notifications are configurable for Discord, Slack, Shoutrrr, Gotify, and Healthchecks. Storage can be any restic backend (S3, B2, Azure, GCS, local, SFTP) or any rclone remote. It is distributed as a standalone Go binary that needs restic, which it downloads automatically if not present.
use_cases: Scheduled backups of home or NAS data
Browsing and restoring files from restic snapshots
Managing existing restic repositories through a web interface
Backing up to S3, B2, SFTP, or rclone remotes
Getting backup success or failure notifications via Discord, Slack, or Gotify
Running backups in Docker or on a NAS
how_to_run: brew tap garethgeorge/homebrew-backrest-tap && brew install backrest && brew services start backrest
docker run via the Docker Compose example using image ghcr.io/garethgeorge/backrest:latest on port 9898
Build: (cd webui && pnpm i && pnpm run build) then (cd cmd/backrest && go build .)
notable: Web UI wraps restic while still allowing direct restic CLI access for advanced use
Single lightweight binary; restic is downloaded automatically if not installed
Opinionated cron-style scheduling of snapshots and repo health operations
Works with all restic storage backends and any rclone remote
Runs on Linux, macOS, Windows, FreeBSD, and Docker
caveats: Windows and macOS have extra setup steps, such as granting Full Disk Access on macOS
The Arch AUR package is third-party and not maintained by the Backrest project
Default bind is localhost only; remote access requires changing BACKREST_PORT or using the --allow-remote-access flag
keywords: back up my files to cloud storage
